definitions.explanation: Prefix attached to a noun to mean 'the entire' or 'all of'. Common in formal and journalistic vocabulary expressing comprehensive scope.

examples.japanese: {全|ぜん}{国民|こくみん}に{呼|よ}びかける。
この{店|みせ}は{全|ぜん}{商品|しょうひん}が{半額|はんがく}になっている。
examples.english: At this shop all products are half price.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{改革|かいかく}は{全|ぜん}{社員|しゃいん}の{働|はたら}き{方|かた}に{影響|えいきょう}する。
examples.english: This reform will affect the working style of all employees.

notes:
Prefix expressing totality, attached to nouns to mean 'all' or 'entire'. Most often appears in compound nouns of Sino-Japanese origin and in formal or written contexts.

COMPOUNDS:
- {全|ぜん}{国|こく}: the whole country
- {全|ぜん}{員|いん}: all members; everyone
- {全|ぜん}{世界|せかい}: the whole world
- {全|ぜん}{社員|しゃいん}: all employees
- {全|ぜん}{商品|しょうひん}: all products
- {全|ぜん}{校|こう}: the whole school
- {全|ぜん}{種類|しゅるい}: all kinds

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全部|ぜんぶ}: all; the whole — stand-alone noun/adverb
- {総|そう}〜: total; gross — emphasizes the aggregate sum ({総|そう}{売|う}り{上|あ}げ total sales)
- {皆|みな}: everyone — refers specifically to people, conversational
